title: The Bank Outage May Have Nothing to Do With Your Bank
gist: A Nov 16, 2026 multi-bank disruption appears traced to a non-cyber software bug in JPMorganChase's on-premise hardware, spilling over to counterparties and Zelle users while Zelle, Visa, Mastercard and others said their systems were normal. It capped a week of major outages including a 24-hour Microsoft 365 failure and an FAA nationwide ground stop.

insights.claim: On Monday Nov 16, 2026, customers of many major US banks, credit unions, fintech apps and card companies reported access problems, with Downdetector reports beginning around 9:30 am ET and peaking around 2 pm ET.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: A single-day, multi-institution disruption is a reminder of payments-system fragility; watch for regulatory scrutiny of bank operational resilience.
insights.locator: Apparent issues with the banks, credit unions

insights.claim: JPMorganChase attributed its disruption to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems and said there was no evidence of a cyberattack.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Legacy on-prem infrastructure risk at the largest US bank may accelerate modernization/cloud migration spend; rules out a cyber narrative for security stocks.
insights.quote: JPMorganChase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems—there is no evidence this is cyber-related
insights.locator: JPMorganChase has experienced a temporary issue

insights.claim: JPMorganChase, the top US retail bank holding over 10 percent of all US deposits, is the likely source of the broad banking disruption, illustrating how a single dominant bank's failure can propagate to counterparties.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Concentration of deposits creates systemic operational single points of failure — a theme for regulators and for counterparty banks.
insights.locator: It is currently unclear which systems

insights.claim: JPMorganChase denied a systemic issue but acknowledged other banks may have seen slower transactions to the extent they transacted with JPMorganChase, while its customers retained access to accounts and funds.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Spillover through transaction counterparty links means a single bank's IT glitch shows up as industry-wide slowness.
insights.quote: other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us

insights.claim: Zelle said its systems were not down and that it does not hold consumer funds, attributing user-facing Zelle problems to the participating banks that manage accounts.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Zelle's dependency on member-bank uptime means P2P payment reliability is only as strong as the weakest large participant.
insights.quote: Zelle is not down. Zelle is operating as it should

insights.claim: US Bank said its systems were not directly impacted but warned clients sending or receiving Zelle payments with other institutions could see transaction delays.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Shows interbank P2P rails transmit delays even to unaffected banks.
insights.quote: clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays

insights.claim: Mastercard, Visa, Capital One and Bank of America all stated their networks and systems were operating normally during the Monday disruption, with Mastercard saying Downdetector reports about it were not correct.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Card networks appear insulated from the incident; limited direct impact on V/MA volumes.

insights.claim: Downdetector outage data relies on user reports rather than official statements and can misattribute outages, as seen with reports implicating Wells Fargo, TD Bank and others during a JPMorganChase-related incident.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Treat crowd-sourced outage trackers as noisy signals before trading on 'outage' headlines about specific firms.

insights.claim: Microsoft 365 suffered an unprecedented 24-hour outage the prior Thursday affecting Outlook, Teams and other cloud services, which Microsoft tied to an update that began rolling out in July but only started causing problems that week.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Latent-update failures in hyperscale SaaS raise questions about change-management and SLA exposure for Microsoft.
insights.quote: Microsoft 365 experienced an unprecedented 24-hour outage that impacted millions of people, governments, businesses, and other institutions globally

insights.claim: The FAA issued a nationwide five-hour ground stop after legacy air-traffic-control communications equipment became unstable when the FAA FTI network was flooded with 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds, cancelling thousands of flights.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Aging government infrastructure is a recurring failure point, supporting the case for ATC modernization spending; airlines bear disruption costs.
insights.quote: The FAA’s legacy equipment became unstable when data began flooding the FAA FTI network, at a rate of 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds
insights.locator: Soon after Microsoft resolved its outage

insights.claim: Back-to-back outages at Microsoft 365, the FAA and major US banks within a week invite speculation of a broader pattern, though each was attributed to a separate, non-cyber technical cause.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Clustered outages heighten perceived systemic tech fragility — watch for resilience regulation and IT modernization demand rather than a single cyber catalyst.
insights.quote: the timing of the issues may as well have been designed to get people looking for broader patterns
